body:
IDENTITY: I am `codex-mockup-science-review`, an independent read-only reviewer. I inspected `storyatlas4s/mockups/mockup1.png` at original resolution and checked its claims against the admitted Boas/Cultee source, the WOG acceptance fixture, ADR 0002 D9-D11, `AlignState`, and `MemoryAddress`. I agree with the owner disposition: this is a useful composition sketch, not model output and not an evidentiary prototype.

WHAT THE SKETCH PROVES USEFULLY

- The shared focus window across overview, Codex, feature tracks, Atlas, and recall is immediately understandable.
- The scene navigator plus exact-text region plus inspector is the right shape for an audit loop.
- The source/recall detail face makes many-to-one mappings more tangible than the current tracer.

SCIENTIFIC ACCEPTANCE FINDINGS

S1 — the displayed observational axis is demonstrably not the admitted source. The checked WOG fixture has sentence ordinals 0–49. The archived admitted file has 553 words including its provenance header, while the story body is shorter. The mockup claims `Words 942–1056` and `Evidence: Sentences 98–104`; those coordinates cannot resolve into this source. This is stronger than a paraphrase concern: the page cannot satisfy a source-offset round trip. A revision titled *The War of the Ghosts* must compile exact text and real source ids, or every pane must be visibly labelled `SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER — NOT SOURCE OR MODEL OUTPUT`.

S2 — the replacement prose changes the scientific object. The source says `He thought they were really people`, later `Now he thought: Oh, they are ghosts`, and later still reports deaths inside his recounting at home. The mockup substitutes direct perception (`saw that the enemy were not men`), invented phenomenal content (`pale figures moving in the mist`), invented action and affect (`brandishing their weapons`, `defended themselves bravely`, `fought ... not showing fear`, `ghosts withdrew`), and a root-world event (`The ghosts struck many of the warriors`). These additions would themselves manufacture the auditory, visual, tension, fear, goal, and recall patterns the panels purport to measure. They are not harmless copy.

S3 — context and epistemic status are collapsed exactly where this story is diagnostic. `Ghosts (revealed)` is drawn as an event and `Ghosts (antagonist)` as a participant, while the accepted model keeps one warrior group and scopes the ghosts attribute to the young man’s belief. `He thought they were really people` and `Now he thought ... ghosts` are belief-state changes, not an objective entity replacement. The reported injury belongs to warrior speech; the later casualties belong to the young man’s nested recounting. A revision needs visible context chrome on node, edge, and text support, plus a persistent `ReaderAt` versus omniscient horizon. A later reinterpretation may add a retrospective portal; it may not rewrite the earlier epistemic state.

S4 — several marks are unsupported interpretive imports. `Prove himself as a warrior`, `The elders worry about disappearances`, and the episode label `Call to Adventure` inject motive, offstage mental state, and a Hero’s-Journey schema absent from the source. `Near Kalama` weakens `on the other side of Kalama`; `war cries` as a cause of the attack is at most a temporal/signal relation, not an evidenced cause. Such a schema could be a named analyst hypothesis lens, but then every mark needs provider, claim id, evidence or upstream claims, alternatives, and `Hypothesized` styling. It cannot be default story structure.

S5 — the map legend and ontology disagree. Purple is declared `Location`, yet `The elders worry about disappearances` is purple; orange is `Event`, yet `Ghosts (revealed)` reads as an entity/status; `Young man is chosen` hides who chooses him and whether this is event, passive state, or inference. This is not merely colour polish: a selectable mark would resolve to the wrong narrative kind. The next artifact should be generated from typed primitives, and its textual twin should make the same mismatch testable without sight.

S6 — the inspector bundles independent claims under one ungrounded number. Event identity, `Type: Conflict`, participant roles, protagonist/antagonist labels, `Intensity: High`, `Outcome: Mixed`, temporal placement, location, two causal links, and a broad evidence window all appear to inherit `Confidence: 0.89`. Those fields can have different evidence, statuses, alternatives, and providers. `0.89` is also ambiguous between an uncalibrated raw credence and a calibrated probability. The inspector should expose a claim per field/relation; raw score and probability must use different labels and scales, and a probability must name its calibration model.

S7 — every quantitative surface currently reads as fabricated complete data. Sentiment, tension, auditory, visual, kinesthetic, recall coverage, recall precision, misordering, omissions, `Intensity: High`, and the heat washes expose no feature space, target grain, unit, reducer, window basis, coverage, missingness, normalization, provider, or derivation receipt. Continuous filled tracks visually assert coverage everywhere. ADR D9–D11 already provide the remedy: magnitude, coverage, missingness, raw credence, calibrated probability, alternatives, and exclusion require distinct channels; window smoothing must come from a named `FeatureDerivation`, not UI interpolation.

S8 — the population-style curves do not define an estimand. `Recall Coverage (avg)`, `Recall Precision (average)`, `Misordering (average)`, and `Omissions (average)` need at minimum subject count, unit of averaging, weighting, denominator, treatment of unranked/abstaining and contentless subjects, support/coverage, uncertainty, and the exact view/model fingerprint. `Precision` in particular is ambiguous: it could mean localization sharpness, fidelity, or an information-retrieval statistic. A polished curve without these fields could manufacture apparent group differences by silently excluding uncertain mass.

RECALL AND MEMORY SEMANTICS

R1 — `Exact` is false even within the mockup: `then they heard yelling` is a paraphrase, not exact text. The known-source vocabulary is `AlignState.Source` for faithful anchored mass and `AlignState.Distorted(ref, facets)` for anchored contradiction. Verbatim identity, semantic faithfulness, and posterior localization are three different claims.

R2 — `Partial / Gist` merges unrelated structures. Gist is mass on a `Segment` anchor; a partial mapping may instead be a split posterior, a blend across anchors, low localizability, or missing facets. These need distinct encodings and descent paths.

R3 — `Misordered` is not a row destination or link class. It is a sequence/transition property visible as a backward transition in `TransitionFlow`. The crossed red arrows can be a route overlay, but they must not replace the row posterior or imply that one alignment cell itself is misordered.

R4 — omission is source-side low `columnMass`, not a recall utterance. Rendering `[skipped]` inside the participant transcript fabricates participant text. Show an empty destination lane or source-side omission mark with the named threshold and uncertainty; preserve the exact recall rail unchanged.

R5 — `External / irrelevant` collapses six scientifically different destinations: Association, Commentary, SourceConsistentInference, Intrusion, Uninterpretable, and Unranked. `Unranked` describes provider abstention, never the rememberer; source-consistent inference may be highly relevant; intrusion is not commentary. The view must preserve the full external state and row mass. It also needs a capacity case for multimodal source mass, distortion facets, and unbalanced rows; clean equal-width arrows cannot establish any of those.

R6 — the visible recall sentences are invented and are not present in the registered fixture. Label them as synthetic diagnostic utterances. If `Participant Recall` means actual participant data, the artifact is barred until the owner records the required redistribution/REB basis and a privacy witness permits the payload. `example` is not a sufficient data-class label.

R7 — do not map this known-source panel onto `MemoryAddress`. `AlignState` answers where a recall unit maps in a known story and with what fidelity. `MemoryAddress` answers where an autobiographical detail may belong: Episode with TargetSpecific/OtherSpecific/Extended/RepeatedOrCategoric scope, PersonalKnowledge, GeneralKnowledge, Discourse, or Unresolved, as a distribution. An AI view therefore needs the exact two-speaker transcript as its observational rail and `DetailAssessment × MemoryAddress` as its default matrix; internal/external is only a declared scoring-policy overlay. `MemoryAddress.Unresolved`, `AlignState.External(Unranked)`, omission, and irrelevance are not synonyms and must never share one mark.

MINIMUM SCIENTIFIC REVISION

Use exact WOG source and real ids; label any recall as synthetic; make the horizon and context frame persistent; replace the graph with one projection contract; show one receipted feature plus explicit missingness; render a matrix-first alignment face preserving full row mass and all external states; never insert `[skipped]` into recalled text; and make the inspector field-addressable rather than assigning one confidence to a bundle. Until then, retain this PNG only as a speculative layout reference.
